# A modal dialog destroyed without close() takes its mask along

Owned: a leaf of #21367 (Dialogs group) until its lock, Sun 22 Nov 18:00 CET.

## Context

Maryam's approval of PR #21417 named the path: `component.Base#destroy()` bypasses `close()` and `unmount()`, so a modal dialog its owner destroys directly never releases its mask. Reproduced in `examples/dialog` on `dev` after #21417, with Modal checked:

```
Create Dialog              -> #neo-dialog-1 (neo-modal), .neo-dialog-modal-mask visible
destroyNeoInstance('neo-dialog-1')
after 1.5 s                -> #neo-dialog-1 gone, .neo-dialog-modal-mask display:block,
                              elementFromPoint(page centre) = .neo-dialog-modal-mask
```

The page stays blocked behind a mask with no dialog over it.

## The Problem

`dialog.Base#close()` releases the mask itself, `syncModalMask(me.id, false)` before `destroy(true)` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:529-532`). Every other way out skips it. An owner that destroys its modal dialog, or a container destroying its items, leaves the mask over the page.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `src/dialog/Base.mjs:529`, "The mask leaves with the dialog". #21415 made that true for `close()` only.

- `Neo.main.DomAccess#syncModalMask({id, modal: false})` places the mask under the topmost remaining modal and leaves the departing id out (#21417), so it is safe to call while the node is still on the page.
- `component.Base#destroy` (`src/component/Base.mjs:1437`) is the one exit every teardown takes; `close()` reaches it too.

## The Fix

- `src/dialog/Base.mjs`: a `destroy()` override releases the mask of a mounted modal dialog, then calls `super.destroy()`. `close()` drops its own `syncModalMask(me.id, false)`, which `destroy(true)` now runs.
- A unit or component spec: a mounted modal dialog destroyed directly leaves no mask over the page.

## Decision Record impact

none

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A mounted modal dialog destroyed without `close()` releases the modal mask: no mask stays over the page, and a modal dialog beneath it keeps its mask.
- [ ] AC-2: `close()` keeps releasing the mask before the dialog leaves, through the same path.

## Out of Scope

- Focus hand-back on a direct destroy: `component.Base#destroy` already runs `revertFocusOnDeparture()`.
- `closeAction: 'hide'` consumers (`desktop.WindowManager`, `board.CardEditor`, `timeline.EventEditor`): hide already syncs the mask.

## Avoided Traps

- **A release in each owner that destroys a dialog.** Every new owner would need to know it; the dialog owns its mask.
